problem: A teacher gives you a test with a set of fifteen questions, out of which you are told to answer ten. How many ways can you answer ten different questions?

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Combinations of Objects Chosen From a Group of at Least Ten
examples.problem: Suppose a teacher needs to select a group of $4$ students from a class of $20$ students to represent the class in a competition. How many different ways can the teacher form a team of $4$ students?
examples.worked_solution:
The number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_nC_r = \dfrac{n!}{(n-r)!r!}.
$$

There are $20$ students, so $n=20.$ We want to select $4$ of those students to form a group, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different ways in which the teacher can form the team is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{20}{C}_{4} & =\frac{20!}{(20-4)!4!} \\  & =\frac{20!}{16!4!} \\  & =\frac{20\cdot 19\cdot 18\cdot 17\cdot \cancel{16!}}{\cancel{16!}4!} \\  & =\frac{116\,280}{24} \\  & =4\,845.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Mike has a box containing $5$ parts of a toy car. In how many ways can Mike select a set of $3$ different parts from the box?
feedback.worked_solution:
The number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $5$ parts in the box, so $n=5.$ We want to select $3$ of those parts, so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of different potential sets of $3$ parts is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{5}{C}_{3} & =\frac{5!}{(5-3)!\,3!} \\  & =\frac{5!}{2!3!} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 4\cdot \cancel{3!}}{2!\cdot \cancel{3!}} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 4}{2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{20}{2} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$
